one_month_reasoning: No earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 results come in early December, after 2026-10-30. The shock (CEO CJ Desai leaving for Meta on 2026-09-28) has already happened. The stock fell from $410 (Friday 9/25 close) to an intraday low near $300, then rebounded to $356 after the investor day, a reaffirmed Q3/FY guide (Q3 revenue $756-761M) and a $1B buyback add. Scheduled events inside the window: FOMC Oct 27-28, where Polymarket had a 25bp hike at ~67% (Sept 26, ~$1.3M 24h volume). That is mostly priced in, but a hawkish surprise with the 10Y at ~5.17% hurts long-duration software. Unscheduled: news on a permanent CEO (a strong external or insider pick is upside; a long search is a slow drag). Short-horizon regularities pull both ways. The rebound from the sharp gap-down may continue partway back toward the $400s, but studies find CEO-departure events raise volatility and have mixed drift. Net: I centre near today's price (median ~$357) with a ~18% monthly sigma, close to annual vol/3.5 = 20%, trimmed slightly because no earnings print falls in the window.

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM sales (8x on ~$4.2B NTM revenue at Sept 2027 plus ~$2.6B net cash -> ~$423), P/E (42x ~$9.00 NTM non-GAAP EPS -> ~$378) and FCF yield (32x ~$850M FY29 FCF plus cash -> ~$350), weighted 40/35/25 -> ~$390.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at 2027-09-30 ~$4.2B x 8.0x EV/sales = $33.6B EV + ~$2.6B net cash = $36.2B / ~85.5M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Management's 3-year target is >20% total growth with Atlas growing mid-20s; Q2 grew 30%. I use 21%: FY28 ~$3.65B, and NTM at Sept 2027 ~ FY28 x 1.15 ~ $4.2B.

Today's EV (~$28.1B) over NTM revenue (~$3.35B) is ~8.4x. MDB's trailing EV/sales has a 5-year average of ~14x, a median of ~12x and a low of ~10x. With the 10Y at 5.2% and the Fed hiking, I hold the multiple slightly below today's level rather than letting it revert to the history.
$2.4B cash and short-term investments at 7/31/26. I add ~$0.7B of FCF, less part of the $2B-plus buyback.
Q2 non-GAAP net income $162.6M / $1.90 per fully diluted share = ~85.6M. I assume buybacks offset SBC dilution.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sept 2027 ~$9.00 x 42x

inputs_detail.derivation: ~21% revenue growth plus 100-200bp of yearly operating-margin expansion (investor-day target) gives EPS growth of ~22%: FY28 ~$7.9, FY29 ~$9.6. NTM at Sept 2027 is a blend, ~$9.0.
The stock trades at ~49x NTM non-GAAP EPS today (356/~7.3) and has been quoted near 51x forward. I compress it to 42x as growth normalises toward 20% under restrictive rates.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY29 FCF ~$850M x 32x (3.1% yield) = $27.2B + $2.6B cash / 85.5M shares

inputs_detail.value: >$1B implied at the midpoint of LT targets

inputs_detail.derivation: Interpolated between run-rate FCF (Q2 $137.6M, roughly $0.6-0.7B for FY27) and the >$1B FY30 implied target.
A 3.1% FCF yield for a ~20% grower with heavy SBC. The 10Y at 5.17% argues against a higher multiple.

bear.story: The CEO search drags and a second leadership transition in a year slows sales execution. Hyperscaler document-DB competition and a macro slowdown (Fed hiking, 10Y >5%) take Atlas growth to high teens. The multiple falls to ~5-6x NTM sales, like the 2025 tariff-shock trough near $140-215 on lower numbers.

base.story: Growth of ~20-22% continues with 100-200bp of margin expansion. A credible permanent CEO (or Ittycheria staying) settles the leadership question. The multiple is roughly unchanged, so the stock tracks earnings and buybacks toward fair value.

bull.story: AI and agent workloads (Atlas Agent Engine, Atlas Infinite, 9.0) keep Atlas near 29-30% growth, the $2B buyback shrinks the share count, and the multiple re-rates toward the ~10-12x historical median. That is consistent with the street-high targets of $525-565.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$240 (about -33%, past the 52-week low region of $216-250 reached in the March-April 2026 selloff), the market would be pricing Atlas growth falling to the mid-teens or a failed leadership transition, not ordinary 70%-vol noise. That would be ~5.5x NTM sales, a level MDB has only reached on real fundamental or macro breaks (2022 and 2025 drawdowns of -65% and -51%).

key_uncertainties: Who becomes permanent CEO and whether sales leadership stays intact after two CEO changes in 11 months
Whether Atlas holds near 27-30% growth or slows toward the >20% long-term target
Rates: Fed hiking with the 10Y ~5.2% could compress high-multiple software further
Competitive pressure from hyperscaler-native databases and Postgres/AI-native stores
Macro: Kalshi prices a 2027 recession at ~20-24%, and MDB's consumption revenue is cyclical
reasoning: Base rates first. MDB is a 70%-realized-vol name. Its drawdowns in past market shocks average -32% against -17% for the S&P 500 (-65% in 2022, -51% in 2025), and it has moved 20-30% on single earnings prints and events. The 52-week range of $216-473 shows how wide a year can be. I therefore use a lognormal sigma of ~0.55: below realized vol, because realized vol is inflated by the recent CEO shock and earnings gaps, and above a typical large cap's 25-35%. The event base rate: the literature finds negative announcement returns and higher subsequent volatility after unexpected CEO resignations, but no consistent long-run underperformance when the departure is voluntary and the business is intact. Here the CEO left for a bigger job (Meta), not over performance. Guidance was reaffirmed, the ex-CEO of 11 years is interim, and the stock has already retraced about half the drop ($410 -> ~$300 -> $356). Fundamentals: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 30% (Atlas 29%), FY27 was raised to $3.01B at the midpoint, the non-GAAP op margin is ~24%, and investor-day targets are >20% growth with 100-200bp of yearly margin expansion. My blended fair value is ~$390 (EV/sales $423, P/E $378, FCF $350), about 10% upside. Consensus targets of ~$457-479 are evidence of sell-side optimism, not my anchor. The macro headwind is real: Polymarket prices further Fed hikes (Oct ~67%, Dec ~72%, a 2026 cut only ~3%), the 10Y is at 5.17% and Kalshi 2027 recession odds are ~20-24%, all of which cap multiple expansion. The scenarios (bear 230/25%, base 390/50%, bull 540/25%) give a mean of ~$388. I set the ladder median at ~$372, a modest drift above spot that reflects fair value partly discounted for leadership risk, with a slightly thinned far right tail. Research was limited to ~10 queries; the Twelve Data estimates endpoint was unavailable on this plan.
